rashi.eng: *saws, and under harrows of iron.* It is grooved with numerous indentations and is called lime [in French]. They are types of tortures.

rashi.heb:
*מגרה.* 
סכין פגום פגימות הרבה תכופות זו לזו:
rashi.eng: *saws.* A knife indented with numerous consecutive nicks.

rashi.heb:
*חריצים.* 
הוא מורג חרוץ מלא חריצים, כמין פצירה פים שקורין לימ"א:
rashi.eng: *harrows.* A threshing sledge. It is grooved with numerous indentations and is called lime [in French].

rashi.heb:
*במלבן.* 
בטיט חוצות, וכן תרגם יונתן: וגרר יתהון בשוקיא.
rashi.eng: *brick kiln.* in the mud of the streets. And so did I translate it: and they dragged them in the streets.

notes.421: (tn, Heb): “Amnon the son of David loved her.” The following verse indicates the extreme nature of his infatuation, so the translation uses “madly in love” here. Amnon was the half-brother of Tamar; Absalom was her full blood-brother.

rashi.heb:
*ולאבשלום אחות יפה.* 
שהיתה בת אמו:
rashi.eng: *a fair sister whose name was Tamar.* who was the daughter of his mother.

notes.422: (tn, Heb): “and there was distress to Amnon so that he made himself sick.”

rashi.heb:
*להתחלות.* 
עד שנחלה:
rashi.eng: *making himself sick.* until he took sick.

rashi.heb:
*כי בתולה היא.* 
צנועה בבית ואינה יוצאת לחוץ, לפיכך ויפלא בעיני אמנון וגו', נכסה ונעלם ממנו מה תואנה יכול לבקש וישכב עמה, כמו (דברים יז ח): כי יפלא ממך, ארי יתכסי ממך:
rashi.eng: *for she was a virgin.* and was hidden within the house, refusing to go outside. Consequently: “it seemed difficult in Amnon’s eyes, etc.” It was concealed and hidden from him what excuse he would be able to seek to lie with her. [This is] similar to: כי יפלא ממך : (Deut. 17:8) which Onkelos translates: “if it be hidden from you.”

rashi.heb:
*איש חכם.* 
לרשעה:
rashi.eng: *sly man.* for evil.

notes.424: (tn): An more idiomatic translation might be “Why are you of all people…?”

rashi.heb:
*דל.* 
כחוש, כמו (בראשית מא יט): דלות ורעות תואר:
rashi.eng: *thin.* lean, similar to: “lean and ill-formed” (Gen. 41:19).

notes.425: (tn): This verb is used in the Hitpael stem only in this chapter of the Hebrew Bible. With the exception of v. 2 it describes not a real sickness but one pretended in order to entrap Tamar. The Hitpael sometimes, as here, describes the subject making oneself appear to be of a certain character. On this use of the stem, see GKC 149-50 �54.e.

rashi.heb:
*את הבריה.* 
את הסעודה:
rashi.eng: *the food.* Heb. הבריה, a light meal.

rashi.heb:
*ותלבב.* 
ותחלוט, סולת מורבכת במים רותחין תחלה, ואחר כך בשמן:
rashi.eng: *and she prepared the dumplings.* She scalded. Fine flour scalded first with boiling water and afterwards with oil.

notes.429: (tc): A few medieval Hebrew mss have “and they removed everyone” (Hiphil preterite with vav consecutive 3cp, rather than Qal preterite with vav consecutive 3cp).

rashi.heb:
*את המשרת.* 
תרגום של מחבת, מסריתא:
rashi.eng: *the pan.* Heb. משרת. The Targum of מחבת [a shallow pan Lev. 2:5] is מסריתא.

notes.430: (tn, Heb): “lie with me” (so NAB, NASB, NRSV); NCV “come and have sexual relations with me.”

notes.431: (tn, Heb): “and you will be like one of the fools.”

rashi.heb:
*כי לא ימנעני ממך.* 
שמותרת אני לך, לפי שנתעברה בי אמי כשהיא נכרית יפת תואר, שלקחה דוד במלחמה, ומי שיש לו בן או בת מן שפחה, אינו בנו לכל דבר:
rashi.eng: *for he will not withhold me from you.* For I am permissible to you since my mother conceived me when she was yet a gentile, a beautiful woman which David had taken in battle. Now whoever has a son or daughter from a [gentile] maidservant he is not considered his son in any respect.

notes.434: (tn, Heb): “and he humiliated her and lay with her.”

notes.435: (tn, Heb): “and Amnon hated her with very great hatred.”
notes.436: (tn, Heb): “for greater was the hatred with which he hated her than the love with which he loved her.”

rashi.heb:
*וישנאה אמנון.* 
אמרו רבותינו (סנהדרין כא א): נימא נקשרה לו, ועשאתו כרות שפכה:
rashi.eng: *And Amnon hated her with very great hatred.* She attached a hair to him and made him into one that is mutilated at the membrum.

notes.437: (tn, Heb): “No, because this great evil is [worse] than the other which you did with me, by sending me away.” Perhaps the broken syntax reflects her hysteria and outrage.

rashi.heb:
*אל אודות.* 
אל תעשה אודות הרעה הזאת של שילוח, הגדולה מן האחרת שעשית עמי ועניתני, ועוד תוסיף רעה ממנה לשלחני:
rashi.eng: *do not.* Do not do this evil act of sending [me] away which is greater [in it’s wickedness] than the other [act] that you had done with me by forcing me for you will only add an even greater wrong than it by sending me away.

notes.438: (tn, Heb): “send this [one] from upon me to the outside.”

notes.439: (tn): The Hebrew expression used here (כְּתֹנֶת פַּסִּים, k�tonet passim) is found only here and in Gen 37:3, 23, 32. Hebrew פַּס (pas) can refer to the palm of the hand or the sole of the foot; here the idea is probably that of a long robe reaching to the feet and having sleeves reaching to the wrists. The notion of a “coat of many colors” (KJV, ASV “garment of divers colors”), a familiar translation for the phrase in Genesis, is based primarily on the translation adopted in the LXX χιτῶνα ποικίλον (citona poikilion) and does not have a great deal of support.
notes.440: (tn, Heb): “his”; the referent (Amnon) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.441: (tn): The Hebrew verb is a perfect with nonconsecutive vav, probably indicating an action (locking the door) that complements the preceding one (pushing her out the door).

notes.442: (tn, Heb): “Don’t set your heart to this thing!”

notes.443: (tc): The LXX and part of the Old Latin tradition include the following addition to v. 21, also included in some English versions (e.g., NAB, NRSV, CEV): “But he did not grieve the spirit of Amnon his son, because he loved him, since he was his firstborn.” Note David’s attitude toward his son Adonijah in 1 Kgs 1:6.

rashi.heb:
*ויהיו גוזזים.*

This emended reading seems also to underlie the translations of the LXX (καὶ ἐβιάσατο, kai ebiasato), the Syriac Peshitta (we’alseh), and Vulgate (cogeret eum).
notes.448: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the king) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.449: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (David) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*ולא ילך נא אתנו.* 
ואם לא יכול אתה ללכת, ילך נא עמנו אמנון:
rashi.eng: *If not, please let… go with us.* If you cannot go, please let Amnon go with us.

notes.451: (tn, Heb): “when good is the heart of Amnon with wine.”

notes.453: (tn, Heb): “it was placed on the mouth of Absalom.”
notes.454: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Amnon) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*על פי אבשלום היתה שומה.* 
בציויו של אבשלום היתה שימה זו נישומת על עבדיו, להרוג את אמנון:
rashi.eng: *by the mouth of Absalom this had been arranged..* By the command of Absalom this order was placed upon his servants, to kill Amnon.

notes.456: (tn, Heb): “and they lifted their voice and wept.”

notes.458: (tc): The Hebrew text leaves the word “David” to be inferred. The Syriac Peshitta and Vulgate add the word “David.” Most of the Greek tradition includes the words “King David” here.

notes.459: (tc): The translation follows 4QSama in reading רוּחַ הַמֶּלֶךְ (ruakh hammelekh, “the spirit of the king”) rather than the MT דָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ (david hammelekh, “David the king”). The understanding reflected in the translation above is that David, though alienated during this time from his son Absalom, still had an abiding love and concern for him. He longed for reconciliation with him. A rather different interpretation of the verse supposes that David’s interest in taking military action against Absalom grew slack with the passing of time, and this in turn enabled David’s advisers to encourage him toward reconciliation with Absalom. For the latter view, see P. K. McCarter, II Samuel (AB), 344, and cf. CEV.
notes.460: (tn, Heb): “was consoled over Amnon, because he was dead.”

rashi.heb:
*ותכל דוד.* 
הרי זה מקרא קצר, ותכל נפש דוד ; וכן תרגם יונתן: וחמידת נפשא דדוד, כמו (תהלים פד ג): נכספה וגם כלתה, לשון תאוה:
rashi.eng: *and [King] David longed.* This is an incomplete verse [which is meant to be read]: “And the soul of David longed.” Now Targum Jonathan also translates it in this manner: “And the soul of David longed” similar to: “yearned and longed כלתה) (נכספה וגם” (Ps. 84:3), an expression of longing.

rashi.heb:
*כי נחם על אמנון.* 
קבל תנחומין:
rashi.eng: *for he was comforted concerning Amnon.* he accepted consolation.

notes.461: (tn, Heb): “the heart of the king was upon.” The Syriac Peshitta adds the verb ’ethre’i (“was reconciled”).

notes.462: (tn): The Hebrew Hitpael verbal form here indicates pretended rather than genuine action.

rashi.heb:
*וישלח יואב תקועה.* 
אמרו רבותינו (מנחות פה ב): כי שמן זית מצוי שם, לכך חכמה מצויה שם:
rashi.eng: *And Joab sent to Tekoa.* Our Rabbis said, “Because olive oil is found there, [in abundance], wisdom is found there.”

notes.464: (tn, Heb): “put the words in her mouth” (so NASB, NIV).

notes.465: (tc): The translation follows many medieval Hebrew mss in reading וַתַּבֹא (vattavo’, “and she went”) rather than the MT וַתֹּאמֶר (vatto’mer, “and she said”). The MT reading shows confusion with וַתֹּאמֶר later in the verse. The emendation suggested here is supported by the LXX, the Syriac Peshitta, some mss of the Targum, and Vulgate.
notes.466: (tn): The word “me” is left to be inferred in the Hebrew text; it is present in the Syriac Peshitta and Vulgate.

rashi.heb:
*אבל אשה אלמנה אני.* 
אבל, בקושטא:
rashi.eng: *truly I am… a widow.* Heb. אבל, in truth.

notes.468: (tn): Here and elsewhere (vv. 7, 12, 15a, 17, 19) the woman uses a term which suggests a lower level female servant. She uses the term to express her humility before the king. However, she uses a different term in vv. 15b-16. See the note at v. 15 for a discussion of the rhetorical purpose of this switch in terminology.

notes.469: (tn, Heb): “in exchange for the life.” The Hebrew preposition בְּ (b�, “in”) here is the so-called bet pretii, or bet (בְּ) of price, defining the value attached to someone or something.
notes.470: (sn): My remaining coal is here metaphorical language, describing the one remaining son as her only source of lingering hope for continuing the family line.

rashi.heb:
*עלי אדני המלך העון.* 
כנוי הוא לכבודו, כלומר אתה מדחה אותי לאמר אני מצוה עליך ואני אלך לדרכי, ואתה לא תצוה עלי, ובני יהרג, על מי העון הזה:
rashi.eng: *on me be the iniquity.* It is a euphemism out of respect for him as if to say: You are putting me off by saying: I will give orders about you. Now if I go on away and you do not give orders about me, upon whom then will the iniquity be?

notes.472: (tn): The words “in that case” are not in the Hebrew text, but may be inferred from the context. They are supplied in the translation for the sake of clarification.

rashi.heb:
*יזכר נא המלך את ה'.* 
שהקפיד על אורך הדרך להציל נפשות, שנאמר (דברים יט ו): והשיגו כי ירבה הדרך, וזהו מהרבות גואל הדם לשחת, ואתה דוחה אותי:
rashi.eng: *let the king remember the Lord your God.* who concerned Himself with the length of the way [to the refuge cities] in order to save lives, as it is stated: “Lest he [the avenger] overtake him because the way is long” (Deut. 19:6). Now this is the meaning of: “So that the avenger of blood destroy not excessively; and you [still] push me off?”

rashi.heb:
*ולמה חשבתה כזאת.* 
שחשדת לישראל, שיבאו להרוג את השני בלא עדים והתראה:
rashi.eng: *thought such a thing about the people of God..* How have you thought such a thing, i.e., that you suspected Israelites of coming to kill another one with neither witnesses nor [mandatory] warning.

rashi.heb:
*ומדבר המלך הדבר הזה כאשם.* 
והדבר הזה שחרצת לאחרים, שאמרת לי לא יפול משערת בנך ארצה, עכשיו שאגלה לך שאין הדבר הזה אלא על שני בניך, אל תתחרט לאמר דברתי זה כאשם, והנני חוזר בי, לבלתי השיב המלך את אבשלום בנו שנדחה ממנו וברח לו:
rashi.eng: *that the king in speaking this word has done so accidentally.* This thing that you decreed for others, i.e., that which you said to me, “not a hair of your son shall fall,” now that I have made it apparent to you that it all related only to your [own] two sons, do not have regrets saying: I stated this accidentally, and behold I am retracting myself, so that the king shall not [be forced to] bring back his son who was banished from him and fled.

rashi.heb:
*ומדבר המלך.* 
אוקינו"ן פרלטי"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *the king in speaking.* Eknon parlot in French.

notes.475: (tn, Heb): “he devises plans for the one banished from him not to be banished.”

rashi.heb:
*כי מות נמות.* 
ודיינו באותו עונש:
rashi.eng: *for die we must.* And it suffices us with that punishment.

rashi.heb:
*ולא ישא אלהים נפש.* 
איש מן המיתה, לפיכך וחשב המלך מחשבות לבלתי ידח ממנו נדח:
rashi.eng: *and God favors not a soul.* and God favors not a soul of man, from death. Therefore, the king should devise means so that he that is banished, not be [permanently] cast from him.

notes.476: (tc): The LXX (ὄψεταί με, opsetai me) has misunderstood the Hebrew יֵרְאֻנִי (yer�’uni, Piel perfect, “they have made me fearful”), taking the verb to be a form of the verb רָאָה (ra’ah, “to see”) rather than the verb יָרֵא (yare’, “to fear”). The fact that the Greek translators were working with an unvocalized Hebrew text (i.e., consonants only) made them very susceptible to this type of error.
notes.477: (tn): Here and in v. 16 the woman refers to herself as the king’s אָמָה (’amah), a term that refers to a higher level female servant toward whom the master might have some obligation. Like the other term, this word expresses her humility, but it also suggests that the king might have some obligation to treat her in accordance with the principles of justice.

rashi.heb:
*ועתה אשר באתי לדבר אל המלך אדני את הדבר הזה.* 
בכינוי עלי ועל בני:
rashi.eng: *And now, my coming to speak of this thing to the king.* by substituting it on myself and my sons.

rashi.heb:
*כי יראוני העם.* 
הפחידוני מלבקש את אדוני על בנו, פן יכעוס עלי:
rashi.eng: *because the people have made me afraid.* They frightened me from seeking out my lord regarding his son lest he be angry with me.

rashi.heb:
*ותאמר שפחתך אדברה נא.* 
כענין זה, אולי יעשה וגו':
rashi.eng: *I will now speak.* in this fashion, for perhaps [the king] will perform, etc.

notes.479: (tn): Or “will.” The imperfect verbal form can have either an indicative or modal nuance. The use of “perhaps” in v. 15b suggests the latter here.
notes.480: (tn, Heb): “in order to deliver his maid.”
notes.482: (tn, Heb): “from the inheritance of God.” The expression refers to the property that was granted to her family line in the division of the land authorized by God.

rashi.heb:
*כי ישמע המלך להציל את אמתו מכף האיש.* 
הבא להרוג את בני, ולהשמידנו יחד מנחלת אלהים:
rashi.eng: *For the king will hear, to deliver his maidservant from the hand of the man.* who comes to kill my son, and destroy us together from the inheritance of God.

rashi.heb:
*ותאמר שפחתך.* 
מאחר שיצוה המלך עלי, יהיה דברו למנוחה לבני, כי לא ישוב מדברו הטוב, כי כמלאך ה' אדני המלך, ולא יחזירנו כעס ושנאה מדברו הטוב:
rashi.eng: *for comfort.* Once the king has given charge concerning me, his declaration [lit., words] will lead to comfort for my son, since he will not retreat from his word; for ‘as an angel of God so is my lord’ and neither wrath or hatred will retreat him from his favorable statement.

notes.483: (tn, Heb): “Is the hand of Joab with you in all this?”

rashi.heb:
*אם אש.* 
כמו אם יש, כמו היש, וכן (מיכה ו י): עוד האש בית רשע, כמו היש:
rashi.eng: *if anyone can.* Heb. אש. Just like אם יש, if there is anyone, or היש, is there anyone. So with האש ביתרשע (Micha 6:10), “are there yet in the house of the wicked?” which is [identical to] היש.

notes.484: (tn, Heb): “to know all that is in the land.”

rashi.heb:
*לבעבור סבב.* 
לגלגל, עד שיצא דבר בנו של המלך לאור:
rashi.eng: *In order to bring about.* [to allow the story] to evolve until the matter of the king’s son as brought to a favorable conclusion.

rashi.heb:
*ואדני חכם.* 
והבנת כי מאת יואב יצאת:
rashi.eng: *and my lord is wise.* and you [therefore] understand that it came forth from Joab.

rashi.heb:
*אל ידי.*

*אל ידי.* 
אינמי"ש אוש"ט בלע"ז:

*וחמשים איש וגו'.* 
כולם נטולי טחול, וחקוקי כפות רגלים:
rashi.eng: *and fifty men were running before him.* They all had their spleen and the flesh of the soles of their feet cut off.

notes.505: (tn, Heb): “your servant.” So also in vv. 8, 15, 21.

rashi.heb:
*והשכים אבשלום.* 
בכל בקר:
rashi.eng: *And Absalom would rise.* Each morning.

rashi.heb:
*מאחד שבטי ישראל עבדך.* 
משבט פלוני:
rashi.eng: *Of one of the tribes of Israel is your servant.* From such-and-such a tribe.

notes.508: (tn, Heb): “a complaint and a judgment.” The expression is a hendiadys.

rashi.heb:
*והצדקתיו.* 
(חרגום:) ואדינניה בקושטא:
rashi.eng: *I would surely do him justice.* I would judge him righteously.

notes.509: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Absalom) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

notes.512: (tc): The MT has here “forty,” but this is presumably a scribal error for “four.” The context will not tolerate a period of forty years prior to the rebellion of Absalom. The Lucianic Greek recension (τέσσαρα ἔτη, tessara ete), the Syriac Peshitta (’arba’ sanin), and Vulgate (post quattuor autem annos) in fact have the expected reading “four years.” Most English translations follow the versions in reading “four” here, although some (e.g. KJV, ASV, NASB, NKJV), following the MT, read “forty.”

rashi.heb:
*מקץ ארבעים שנה.* 
ששאלו ישראל מלך משמואל, נתגלגל דבר מרד והשפלה במלכות:
rashi.eng: *at the end of forty years.* [from the time] that the Israelites requested a king from Samuel, came about [this] rebellion and drop [of prestige] in the monarchy.

rashi.heb:
*אלכה נא.* 
לחברון:
rashi.eng: *allow me to go, I beg you.* to Hebron.

rashi.heb:
*ואשלם את נדרי.* 
אמרו רבותינו (סוטה לד ב): להביא כבשים מחברון, כי שם היו כבשים שמנים:
rashi.eng: *and pay my vow.* Our Rabbis have stated: “To fetch lambs from Hebron, for there were fat lambs there.”

notes.513: (tn, Heb): “for your servant vowed a vow.” The formal court style of referring to one’s self in third person (“your servant”) has been translated here as first person for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*קרואים והולכים לתמם.* 
מפורש במסכת סוטה ירושלמית (א ח) שבקש מאביו שיכתוב לו, שכל שני בני אדם שיבקש שילכו עמו, ילכו והיה מראה אותו לשנים כאן, ואחר כך לשנים אחרים, וכן הרבה:
rashi.eng: *that were invited and went in their innocence.* It is explained in T.P. Sotah that he requested his father to write for him that any two people that he would ask to go with him, should go, and he showed this [decree] to two people here, then to two others [elsewhere], and so he did many times.

notes.518: (tn): Traditionally, “counselor,” but this term is more often associated with psychological counseling today, so “adviser” was used in the translation instead.
notes.519: (tn, Heb): “Absalom sent for Ahithophel the Gilonite, the adviser of David, from his city, from Giloh, while he was sacrificing.” It is not entirely clear who (Absalom or Ahithophel) was offering the sacrifices.

notes.520: (tn, Heb): “the heart of the men of Israel is with Absalom.”

notes.521: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.
notes.525: (tn, Heb): “and strike the city with the edge of the sword.”

notes.526: (tn, Heb): “according to all that my lord the king will choose, behold your servants!”

rashi.heb:
*בית המרחק.* 
(תרגום:) באתר דרחיק:
rashi.eng: *at the farthest house.* in a distant place.

notes.532: (tn, Heb): “crossing over near the face of.”

rashi.heb:
*על ידו.* 
אצלו, הוא עומד והם עוברים:
rashi.eng: *beside him.* he stood and they passed by.

notes.533: (tn): The word “new” is not in the Hebrew text, but is supplied in the translation to make it clear that David refers to Absalom, not himself.

rashi.heb:
*עם המלך.* 
עם אבשלום:
rashi.eng: *with the king.* with Absalom.

rashi.heb:
*כי נכרי אתה.* 
ואנחנו בורחים מאין צידה ומזון, ומתוך שאתה נכרי לא תמצא מרחמים:
rashi.eng: *for you are a foreigner.* Now we flee without provision or food, and because you are a gentile you will not [readily] find [anyone] to take pity.

rashi.heb:
*וגם גולה אתה למקומך.* 
וגם אם גולה אתה מעם המלך שאינך רוצה להיות עמו, למקומך חזור לך, כי לא טוב לכתך עמי, שהרי תמול באת:
rashi.eng: *and if you are wont to wander, [go to] your own place.* and if you wish to wander from the king because you do not desire to be with him, return to your own place, for your travel with me is not advisable, since [just] yesterday you came.

notes.536: (tn, Heb): “loyal love and truth.” The expression is a hendiadys.

rashi.heb:
*והיום אניעך עמנו.* 
ואין לי מקום שאוכל להושיבך שם ולהמלט, כי אני הולך אל אשר יקרני המקרה ללכת, יום יום כשאשמע שהרודפים כאן, אני בורח כאן, וכן תרגם יונתן 'וגם גולה אתה למקומך': ואף אם גלי את אזיל לך לאתרך:
rashi.eng: *and today I should move you about with us?.* For I have no place where I can settle you so that you be spared, since from day to day, I go wherever chance takes me. When I hear that the pursuers are here, I run there. Now Jonathan also translates אתה למקומך וגם גולה as: and if you are wont to wander, go you to your own place.

rashi.heb:
*חסד ואמת.* 
אני מחזיק בך טובת חסד ואמת שעשית עמדי:
rashi.eng: *kindness and truth.* I thank you for the kindness and truth that you have done with me.

notes.538: (tn, Heb): “whether for death or for life.”

rashi.heb:
*לך ועבור.* 
עם שאר העם, אחר אשר אינך רוצה להפרד ממני:
rashi.eng: *go and pass over.* with the rest of the people, seeing that you do not desire to separate from me.

rashi.heb:
*וכל העם עוברים.* 
מן המלך והלאה, לפי שהוא עומד, קורא אותם עוברים:
rashi.eng: *and all the people passed over.* from the king and on. Since David was standing still, they are referred to as passing over.

rashi.heb:
*ויציקו.* 
כמו ויציגו, (תרגום:) ואקימו ית ארונא, העמידוהו לצד אחד, והעם עוברים, שהיה דוד רוצה לשאתו עמו:
rashi.eng: *set down.* Heb. ויציקו, similar to ויציגו, to set down, [as indicated by Jonathan’s translation]: they set down the ark. They placed it to a side and the people passed by, since David desired to carry it with him.

rashi.heb:
*ויעל אביתר עד תם וגו'.* 
הרי זה מקרא מסורס, ויציקו את ארון האלהים עד תום כל העם לעבור:
rashi.eng: *and Abiathar went up until all the people had finished, etc..* This is an inverted verse: “They set down the ark of God until all the people had finished passing!”

rashi.heb:
*ויעל אביתר.* 
אותו היום נסתלק מן הכהונה, ששאל באורים ותומים ולא נענה, ונכנס צדוק תחתיו וכן שנינו בסדר עולם ובסדר יומא (עג ב):
rashi.eng: *went up.* On that day he [Abiathar] was removed from the [High] Priesthood because he had inquired of the Urim and Tumim but was not answered and Zadok entered in his stead. So we learned in Seder Olam and Seder Yoma.

notes.548: (tn): The Greek tradition understands the Hebrew word as an imperative (“see”). Most Greek mss have ἴδετε (idete); the Lucianic recension has βλέπε (blepe). It could just as well be taken as a question: “Don’t you see what is happening?” The present translation takes the word as a question, with the implication that Zadok is a priest and not a prophet (i.e., “seer”) and therefore unable to know what the future holds.
notes.549: (tn, Heb): “And Ahimaaz your son, and Jonathan the son of Abiathar, two of your sons, with you.” The pronominal suffix on the last word is plural, referring to Zadok and Abiathar.

rashi.heb:
*הרואה אתה.* 
אם רואה אתה שעצה נכונה היא, שוב העיר וגו':
rashi.eng: *Do you [not] see.* If you see that it is a sensible plan then return to the city, etc.

rashi.heb:
*שני בניכם אתכם.* 
בידם תוכלו להודיעני מה שתשמעו מבית המלך, לפי מה שתודיעוני אמלט:
rashi.eng: *Your two sons [shall be] with you.* Through them you can inform me about what you hear from the house of the king, and based on your information I will be able to [plan an] escape.

notes.550: (tn): The pronoun is plural, referring to Zadok and Abiathar.

rashi.heb:
*במעלה הזתים.* 
בהר הזתים:
rashi.eng: *by the ascent of the olives.* by the Mount of Olives.

rashi.heb:
*חפוי.* 
מכורך, כדרך האבלים:
rashi.eng: *his head covered.* wrapped around in the manner of mourners.

rashi.heb:
*חפו.* 
(תרגום:) כריכו:
rashi.eng: *covered.* wrapped.

notes.551: (tc): The translation follows 4QSama, part of the Greek tradition, the Syriac Peshitta, Targum, and Vulgate uldavid in reading “and to David,” rather than MT וְדָוִד (v�david, “and David”). As Driver points out, the Hebrew verb הִגִּיד (higgid, “he related”) never uses the accusative for the person to whom something is told (S. R. Driver, Notes on the Hebrew Text and the Topography of the Books of Samuel, 316).

rashi.heb:
*ודוד הגיד.* 
ולדוד הגיד המגיד:
rashi.eng: *and [someone] told David.* and the informer told to David.

rashi.heb:
*סכל.* 
קלקל, כמו (קהלת י יד): הסכל ירבה דברים:
rashi.eng: *among the conspirators.* Heb. סכל, make foolish frustrated [by making foolish] similar to: “And the fool (והסכל) multiplies his words” (Eccl. 10:14).

rashi.heb:
*בא עד הראש.* 
(תרגום:) עד ריש טוריא:
rashi.eng: *coming to the top.* to the top of the mount.

rashi.heb:
*אשר ישתחוה שם לאלהים.* 
אשר היה רגיל להשתחות שם כשהיה בא לירושלים, היה רואה משם את האהל שהארון בתוכו, והיה משתחוה:
rashi.eng: *where he would prostrate himself to God.* Where he was wont to prostrate himself. When he would come to Jerusalem he would see from there the tent containing the ark and would prostrate himself.

rashi.heb:
*עבד אביך ואני מאז.* 
כמו ואני עבד אביך מאז, ומקרא מסורס הוא:
rashi.eng: *just as I was previously father’s servant.* as if [it were written]: “and I was previously your father’s servant”; for it is an inverted sentence.

notes.554: (tn, Heb): “Will not Zadok and Abiathar the priests be there with you?” The rhetorical question draws attention to the fact that Hushai will not be alone.
notes.555: (tn, Heb): “from the house of the king.”

notes.556: (tn, Heb): “and you must send by their hand to me every word which you hear.” Both of the second person verb forms are plural with Zadok, Abiathar, and Hushai being the understood subjects.

rashi.heb:
*יבוא ירושלים.* 
נתן לבו שיבא לירושלים:
rashi.eng: *(was) coming to Jerusalem.* contemplated coming to Jerusalem.

rashi.heb:
*ומאה קיץ.* 
(תרגום:) ומאה מנן דבילתא:
rashi.eng: *a hundred summer fruit.* Heb. מאה קיץ, a hundred litras of pressed figs.

notes.559: (tc): The translation follows the Qere and many medieval Hebrew mss in reading וְהַלֶּחֶם (v�hallekhem, “and the bread”) rather than וּלְהַלֶּחֶם (ul�hallekhem, “and to the bread”) of the Kethib. The syntax of the MT is confused here by the needless repetition of the preposition, probably taken from the preceding word.

notes.562: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

notes.564: (tn, Heb): “came to.” The form of the verb in the MT is odd. Some prefer to read וַיַּבֹא (vayyavo’), preterite with vav consecutive) rather than וּבָא (uva’), apparently perfect with vav), but this is probably an instance where the narrative offline v�qatal construction introduces a new scene.
notes.565: (tn, Heb): “And look, from there a man was coming out from the clan of the house of Saul and his name was Shimei son of Gera, continually going out and cursing.”

notes.568: (tn, Heb): “What to me and to you?”

rashi.heb:
*כה יקלל.* 
כן יקלל:
rashi.eng: *So let him curse.*

rashi.heb:
*ה' אמר לו.* 
אפשר אדם כמותו שהוא ראש לסנהדרין, יקלל את המלך אם לא שנאמר לו מאת הקב"ה:
rashi.eng: *because the Lord said to him.* Is it possible that a man like him who is the head of the Sanhedrin would curse the king had he not been commanded by the Holy One Blessed be He?

notes.569: (tn, Heb): “who came out from my entrails.” David’s point is that is his own son, his child whom he himself had fathered, was now wanting to kill him.

notes.570: (tc): The Hebrew text is difficult here. It is probably preferable to read with the LXX, the Syriac Peshitta, and Vulgate בְּעוֹנִי (b�’onyi, “on my affliction”) rather than the Kethib of the MT בָּעַוֹנִי (ba’avoni, “on my wrongdoing”). While this Kethib reading is understandable as an objective genitive (i.e., “the wrong perpetrated upon me”), it does not conform to normal Hebrew idiom for this idea. The Qere of the MT בְּעֵינֵי (b�’eni, “on my eyes”), usually taken as synecdoche to mean “my tears,” does not commend itself as a likely meaning. The Hebrew word is one of the so-called tiqqune sopherim, or “emendations of the scribes.”
notes.571: (tn, Heb): “and the Lord will restore to me good in place of his curse this day.”

rashi.heb:
*יראה ה' בעיני.* 
דמעת עיני:
rashi.eng: *the tears of my eyes.* Heb. בעיני, in my eye.

notes.572: (tn, Heb): “and he cursed and threw stones, opposite him, pelting [them] with dirt.” The offline v�qatal construction in the last clause indicates an action that was complementary to the action described in the preceding clause. He simultaneously threw stones and dirt.

notes.573: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (David) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*וינפש שם.* 
בבחורים:
rashi.eng: *refreshed himself there.* in Bahurim.

notes.574: (tn, Heb): “and all the people, the men of Israel.”
notes.575: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

notes.576: (tn, Heb): “to Absalom.” The proper name has been replaced by the pronoun “him” in the translation for stylistic reasons.

notes.577: (tn, Heb): “No for with the one whom the Lord has chosen, and this people, and all the men of Israel, I will be and with him I will stay.” The translation follows the Qere and several medieval Hebrew mss in reading לוֹ (lo, “[I will be] to him”) rather than the MT לֹא (lo’, “[I will] not be”), which makes very little sense here.

notes.578: (tn, Heb): “Just as I served before your father, so I will be before you.”

notes.579: (tn, Heb): “go to”; NAB “have (+ sexual NCV) relations with”; TEV “have intercourse with”; NLT “Go and sleep with.”
notes.580: (tn, Heb): “and the hands of all who are with you will be strengthened.”

rashi.heb:
*וחזקו ידי כל אשר אתך.* 
כי עתה ידם רפה לעזור לך, שאומרים בלבם הבן יתחרט אצל אביו, ואנו נהיה שנואים למלך:
rashi.eng: *Then the hands of all that are with above, you will be strengthened.* For now they [lit., their hands] are lax to support you for they say in their hearts: “the son will have a change of heart when [he is] near his father and we [alone] will remain despised by David.”

notes.581: (sn): That is, on top of the flat roof of the palace, so it would be visible to the public.
notes.582: (tn, Heb): “went to”; NAB “he visited his father’s concubines”; NIV “lay with his father’s concubines”; TEV “went in and had intercourse with.”

notes.583: (tn, Heb): “And the advice of Ahithophel which he advised in those days was as when one inquires of the word of God.”
notes.584: (tn, Heb): “So was all the advice of Ahithophel, also to David, also to Absalom.”

notes.585: (tn, Heb): “and I will come upon him.”

notes.587: (tc, Heb): “like the returning of all, the man whom you are seeking.” The LXX reads differently: “And I will return all the people to you the way a bride returns to her husband, except for the life of the one man whom you are seeking.” The other early versions also struggled with this verse. Modern translations are divided as well: the NAB, NRSV, REB, and NLT follow the LXX, while the NASB and NIV follow the Hebrew text.
notes.588: (tn, Heb): “all of the people will be safe.”

rashi.heb:
*כשוב הכל.* 
אליך:
rashi.eng: *when all shall have returned.* to you.

rashi.heb:
*האיש אשר אתה מבקש.* 
יעשה בו בקשתך ויהרג, ואחר כך כל העם יהיה שלום, וזה מקרא קצר.
rashi.eng: *the man whom you seek.* the man whom you seek, [if] unto him will be done what you desire, and he will be killed, then all the people will be at peace. This is an incomplete verse.

rashi.heb:
*ובעיני זקני ישראל.* 
זקני אשמאי:
rashi.eng: *the elders of Israel.* the uncultured old men of Israel.

notes.590: (tc): In the MT the verb is singular, but in the LXX, the Syriac Peshitta, and Vulgate it is plural.

notes.592: (tn, Heb): “Not good is the advice which Ahithophel has advised at this time.”

notes.593: (tc): The LXX (with the exception of the recensions of Origen and Lucian) repeats the description as follows: “Just as a female bear bereft of cubs in a field.”

rashi.heb:
*ואביך איש מלחמה.* 
ויודע עניני מלחמה וטכסיסיה וטיב מארב, ובטוח הוא שתרדוף הלילה לבא עליו, לפיכך לא ילין עם שאר העם:
rashi.eng: *and your father is a man of war.* who knows the affairs of battle, its arrays, and the science of ambush, and [undoubtedly] trusts that you will [likely] chase at night to come upon him. Therefore he will not lodge with the rest of the people.

notes.594: (tn, Heb): “that he falls on them [i.e., Absalom’s troops] at the first [encounter]; or “that some of them [i.e., Absalom’s troops] fall at the first [encounter].”

rashi.heb:
*הנה עתה הוא נחבא.* 
וכשתבא על מחנה העם אשר אתו, הוא לא יהיה שם שתהרגנו:
rashi.eng: *Behold now he is [surely] hidden.* And when you come upon the campsite of the people with him, he will not be there for you to kill him.

rashi.heb:
*והיה כנפול בהם בתחלה.* 
אני אמרתי לך כי אנשיו גבורים ומרי נפש, ואם יהרגו בעמך, תהיה בם מפלה במלחמה זו שהיא ראשונה, ושמע השומע מכל ישראל הבאים להתחבר אליך, ואמר היתה מגפה בעם של אבשלום:
rashi.eng: *and it will come to pass, if there fall among them at the first.* I have told you that his men are [both] mighty and of embittered spirit. Now if they kill from among your people and they shall be felled in this first battle, then who ever hears from among all the Israelites that come to join you will declare that there has been a massacre among Absalom’s people.

rashi.heb:
*והוא גם בן חיל.* 
ואותו השומע אפילו הוא בן חיל ולבו כלב האריה, המס ימס בפחד ורעדה, ולא יתקשר עוד אליך, כי יאמר כבר התחיל ליפול ונענש הוא על אביו, ולא יצליח:
rashi.eng: *and even if he be valiant.* Even if the one who hears [of it] be valiant, and his heart is as the heart of a lion, he will utterly melt with fear and shudder, and he will no longer band with you, for he will say: He has already begun to decline and he is being punished for [actions towards] his father, and will [therefore] not succeed.

rashi.heb:
*כי יעצתי.* 
כי זאת עצתי:
rashi.eng: *Therefore I counsel.* For this is my counsel.

rashi.heb:
*ופניך הולכים בקרב.* 
בראש, (תרגום:) ואת תהי אזיל בריש כולנא:
rashi.eng: *and you personally go to battle.* at the forefront, and you shall go at the head of all of us.

rashi.heb:
*ונחנו עליו.* 
וננוח עליו, לשון חנייה, כמו (שמות י יד): וינח בכל גבול מצרים, (ישעיהו ז ב): נחה ארם על אפרים:
rashi.eng: *and we shall light upon him.* We shall rest upon him. It is an expression of camping (חנייה), similar to “and they landed (וינח) in all the border of Egypt” (Ex. 10:14); (and) “Aram lights upon (נחה) [Judah] with Ephraim” (Isa. 7:2).

rashi.heb:
*חבלים.* 
(תרגום:) משריין, כמו (שמואל-א י ה): חבל נביאים (תהלים קיט סא): חבלי רשעים:
rashi.eng: *ropes.* Heb. חבלים, bands [battalions], similar to “bands of (חבל) prophets” (I Sam. 10:5) and “bands of (חבלי) wicked men” (Ps. 119:6).

rashi.heb:
*עד הנחל.* 
חומת העיר נסחוב אל הגי:
rashi.eng: *to the valley.* We will drag the walls of the city to the valley.

notes.597: (tn, Heb): “send quickly and tell David saying.”
notes.599: (tn): That is, “cross over the Jordan River.”

rashi.heb:
*וגם עבור תעבור.* 
את הירדן:
rashi.eng: *but pass speedily over.* the Jordan.

rashi.heb:
*פן יבולע למלך.* 
שלא יעצתיו לטובה, ויעשה כדברי אחיתופל:
rashi.eng: *lest the king be destroyed.* Lest the king [Absalom] be told secretly that I did not counsel him well, and he will follow the words of Ahithophel.

rashi.heb:
*יבלע.* 
יאמר לו בסתר ובבליעה:
rashi.eng: *be destroyed.* [The word] יבלע [is to be understood as] it will be told to him in a secretive and concealed [swallowed] manner.

rashi.heb:
*בעין רוגל.* 
(תרגום:) בעין קצרא, כובסי בגדי צמר, שחובטין אותם שם, שבועטים אותם ברגל:
rashi.eng: *En-rogel.* lit. by the launderer’s spring. Launderers of woolen garments would press it there by beating them [the garments] with the(ir) foot.

rashi.heb:
*את המסך.* 
וילון:
rashi.eng: *covering.* a curtain.

rashi.heb:
*הרפות.* 
חטין כתושות, כמו (משלי כז כב): בתוך הריפות:
rashi.eng: *groats.* Heb. הריפות, “crushed wheat” similar to: “amongst the crushed wheat (הריפות)” (Prov. 27:22).

notes.601: (tn, Heb): “they”; the referents (Absalom’s men) have been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.602: (map): For location see Map5-B1; Map6-F3; Map7-E2; Map8-F2; Map10-B3; JP1-F4; JP2-F4; JP3-F4; JP4-F4.

rashi.heb:
*מיכל המים.* 
איני יודע לו פתרון במחברת כל, ופתרונו לפי ענינו, כמו שבולת הנהר:
rashi.eng: *forded the river.* I do not know an interpretation for it in any grouping, and it’s interpretation in keeping with the subject, would be ‘the river current’.

notes.603: (tn, Heb): “they”; the referents (Ahimaaz and Jonathan) have been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.605: (tn, Heb): “for thus Ahithophel has devised against you.” The expression “thus” is narrative shorthand, referring to the plan outlined by Ahithophel (see vv. 1-3). The men would surely have outlined the plan in as much detail as they had been given by the messenger.

notes.606: (tn): The word “River” is not in the Hebrew text here or in v. 24, but has been supplied in the translation for clarity.

notes.607: (tc): The Greek recensions of Origen and Lucian have here “house” for “grave.”

rashi.heb:
*בת נחש.* 
הוא ישי אבי דוד, רבותינו אמרו (בבא בתרא יז א): שמת בלא עון, בעטיו של נחש:
rashi.eng: *the daughter of Nahash.* This is Jesse, David’s father. Our Rabbis stated that he died without sin, only because of the advice of the Serpent (נחש).

rashi.heb:
*ושבי בן נחש.* 
הוא חנון בן נחש:
rashi.eng: *Shobi the son of Nahash.* The same as Hanun the son of Nahash.

notes.610: (tc): The MT adds “roasted grain” וְקָלִי (v�qali) at the end of v. 28, apparently accidentally repeating the word from its earlier occurrence in this verse. With the LXX, the Syriac Peshitta, and an Old Latin ms the translation deletes this second occurrence of the word.

rashi.heb:
*משכב.* 
מצעות:
rashi.eng: *Beds.*

rashi.heb:
*וספות.* 
כלי תשמיש הם, כמו (מלכים . ב יב יד): ספות כסף:
rashi.eng: *bowls.* These are utensils, similar to: “bowls of silver (ספותכסף)” of II Kings 12:14.

rashi.heb:
*וקלי.* 
מיני קליות, אמרו רבותינו (עבודה זרה לח ב): שני מיני שתיתא הקריב ברזילי לדוד, אחד של חטים, ואחד של עדשים, כענין האמור כאן ; 'קמח וקלי', הוא של דגן, 'ופול ועדשים וקלי', ממינים של קטניות שמייבשין אותן בתנור כשהן לחין, והם מתוקין לעולם, וטוחנין אותן, ועושין מהם מאכל שקורין שתיתא:
rashi.eng: *parched grain.* Heb. קלי, types of parched grain. Our Rabbis stated: Two types of flour mixed with honey did Barzillai offer David, one of wheat and the other of lentils, as stated here: “… and wheat and parched grain…” which is of bread stuffs; “and beans and lentils and parched grain…” [which is] of those types of beans that are dried in an oven and remain forever sweet. They are then ground and from them a dish called ‘shatitha’ is made.

notes.611: (tn, Heb): “cheese of the herd,” probably referring to cheese from cow’s milk (rather than goat’s milk).
notes.612: (tn): Or “wilderness” (so KJV, NASB, NRSV, TEV, NLT).

rashi.heb:
*ושפות בקר.* 
(תרגום:) וגובנין דחלב:
rashi.eng: *and cheese of kine.* This follows Jonathan.

notes.615: (tn, Heb): “they will not place to us heart.”
notes.616: (tc): The translation follows the LXX (except for the Lucianic recension), Symmachus, and Vulgate in reading אָתָּה (’atta, “you”) rather than MT עָתָּה (’atta, “now”).

rashi.heb:
*לא ישימו אלינו לב.* 
לא יהיה דבר חשוב בעיניהם להתגבר ולהתהלל, מאחר שאין אתה במלחמה:
rashi.eng: *they will not pay attention to us.* lit., set heart to us. It will not be important to them to overpower us and to boast, since you are not [taking part] in the battle.

rashi.heb:
*כי עתה.* 
בהיותך בכבודך, חשוב אתה כמונו:
rashi.eng: *For now.* with you in your full glory, you are of equal import to us all.

rashi.heb:
*עשרת אלפים.* 
כעשרת אלפים איש כמונו:
rashi.eng: *ten thousand of us.*

rashi.heb:
*כי תהיה לנו מעיר לעזור.* 
(תרגום:) וכען טב ארי תצלי עלנא מן קרתא למסעד:
rashi.eng: *that you be for us from the city as aid.* And now it is better that you pray for us from the city for support.

rashi.heb:
*לאט לי לנער.* 
אם יקרא לפניכם במלחמה, חמלו עליו:
rashi.eng: *deal gently with the youth.* If he chances to come before you in battle, take pity on him.

rashi.heb:
*ביער אפרים.*

notes.633: (tn): There is a play on the word “heart” here that is difficult to reproduce in English. Literally the Hebrew text says “he took three spears in his hand and thrust them into the heart of Absalom while he was still alive in the heart of the oak tree.” This figure of speech involves the use of the same word in different senses and is known as antanaclasis. It is illustrated in the familiar saying from the time of the American Revolution: “If we don’t hang together, we will all hang separately.” The present translation understands “heart” to be used somewhat figuratively for “chest” (cf. TEV, CEV), which explains why Joab’s armor bearers could still “kill” Absalom after he had been stabbed with three spears through the “heart.” Since trees do not have “chests” either, the translation uses “middle.”

notes.677: (tn): Though this verb in the MT is 3rd person masculine singular, it should probably be read as 2nd person masculine singular. It is one of fifteen places where the Masoretes placed a dot over each of the letters of the word in question in order to call attention to their suspicion of the word. Their concern in this case apparently had to do with the fact that this verb and the two preceding verbs alternate from third person to second and back again to third. Words marked in this way in Hebrew manuscripts or printed editions are said to have puncta extrordinaria, or “extraordinary points.”

notes.709: (tn): The expression used here יְמִינִי (y�mini) is a short form of the more common “Benjamin.” It appears elsewhere in 1 Sam 9:4 and Esth 2:5. Cf. 1 Sam 9:1.

notes.711: (tc): The MT reads לְאֹהָלָיו (l�’ohalav, “to his tents”). For a similar idiom, see 19:9. An ancient scribal tradition understands the reading to be לְאלֹהָיו (le’lohav, “to his gods”). *הזעק לי את איש יהודה.* 
שיהו כאן עד שלשה ימים:
rashi.eng: *call together for me the men of Judah.* So that they be here within three days.

rashi.heb:
*ואתה פה עמוד.* 
לסוף שלשת ימים הוי זהיר להיות עומד כאן לפני, כי חפץ היה לרדוף אחרי שבע בן בכרי:
rashi.eng: *then be here present.* After the three days be sure to remain here before me for David desired to pursue Sheba the son of Bichri.

rashi.heb:
*ויוחר מן המועד.* 
אשכחינהו לרבנן דפתחו במסכתא, כדאיתא בסנהדרין (מט א):
rashi.eng: *and he tarried past the set time.* He found the rabbis beginning a tractate, as is found in Sanhedrin.

notes.719: (tn, Heb): “find.” The perfect verbal form is unexpected with the preceding word “otherwise.” We should probably read instead the imperfect. Although it is possible to understand the perfect here as indicating that the feared result is thought of as already having taken place (cf. BDB 814 s.v. פֶּן 2), it is more likely that the perfect is simply the result of scribal error. In this context the imperfect would be more consistent with the following verb וְהִצִּיל (v�hitsil, “and he will get away”).

rashi.heb:
*אתה קח את עבדי אדוניך.* 
אחרי אשר איחר עמשא שר הצבא, ולא הביא את צבא יהודה, קח אתה מן הנמצאים סביבי, ורדוף אחריו:
rashi.eng: *… take your lord’s servants.* Since Amasa has tarried and has not brought the army of Judah, take you from among those that are found around me and pursue him.

rashi.heb:
*והציל עינינו.* 
והציל עצמו מעינינו, והרי זה מקרא קצר:
rashi.eng: *save our eyes.* And save himself before our eyes. Now this is an abbreviated verse.

notes.720: (sn): The significance of the statement it fell out here is unclear. If the dagger fell out of its sheath before Joab got to Amasa, how then did he kill him? Josephus, Ant. 7.11.7 (7.284), suggested that as Joab approached Amasa he deliberately caused the dagger to fall to the ground at an opportune moment as though by accident. When he bent over and picked it up, he then stabbed Amasa with it. Others have tried to make a case for thinking that two swords are referred to – the one that fell out and another that Joab kept concealed until the last moment. But nothing in the text clearly supports this view. Perhaps Josephus’ understanding is best, but it is by no means obvious in the text either.

rashi.heb:
*מצומדת על מתניו.* 
סמוכה מאוד לגופו לרוחב מתניו, שלא כדרך חוגרי חרב, כדי שתהא נוחה ליפול, ולא יצטרך להוציאה מתערה:
rashi.eng: *fastened to his loins.* clinging to his body to the width of his loins and not in a manner that one [customarily] fastens his sword, in order that it should fall easily and not necessitate removal from its sheath…

rashi.heb:
*והוא יצא.* 
כנגד עמשא:
rashi.eng: *and he went forth.* towards Amasa.

rashi.heb:
*ותפול.* 
החרב מתערה, לפי שהיתה חלקה ולטושה, ואינה תלויה לצד ירכו אלא לרוחב מתניו, וכמעט ששח עצמו לצד הארץ, נפלה מתערה ואחזה בימינו, ולא הכיר עמשא בדבר:
rashi.eng: *and it fell out.* i.e., the sword from its sheath, since it was smooth and sharpened and it was not suspended at the side of his hip but [to the] width of his loins. [Thus] almost as soon as he bent toward the ground it fell from its sheath where he grasped it with his right hand without Amasa becoming aware of it.

notes.721: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Joab) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.722: (tn, Heb): “his”; the referent (Amasa) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.723: (tn, Heb): “and he did not repeat concerning him, and he died.”

notes.725: (tn, Heb): “him”; the referent (Amasa) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.726: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (the man who spoke up in v. 11) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.727: (tn, Heb): “Amasa.” For stylistic reasons the name has been replaced by the pronoun (“him”) in the translation.

rashi.heb:
*כאשר ראה כל הבא עליו ועמד.* 
כאשר ראה האיש, שכל הבא עליו היה עומד:
rashi.eng: *when he saw that everyone who came upon him stood still.* When the man saw that everyone who came upon him remained standing [there].

notes.728: (tn, Heb): “him”; the referent (Amasa) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*כאשר הוגה.* 
כאשר הומשך, כמו (משלי כה ד): הגו סיגים מכסף ; וכמו (שם פסוק ה): הגו רשע לפני מלך:
rashi.eng: *when he was removed.* Heb. הגה, when he was taken away, similar to: “take away the dross from the silver (הגו סיגים מכסף)” (Prov. 25:4.), and similar to: “take away the wicked from before the king (הגו רשע לפני מלך)” (ibid. 25:5).

notes.729: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Sheba) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.730: (tc): In keeping with the form of the name in v. 15, the translation deletes the “and” found in the MT.
notes.731: (tc): The translation follows the Qere, many medieval Hebrew mss, and the ancient versions in reading וַיִּקָּהֲלוּ (vayyiqqahalu, “and they were gathered together”) rather than the Kethib of the MT וַיִּקְלֻהוּ (vayyiqluhu, “and they cursed him”). The Kethib is the result of metathesis.

rashi.heb:
*ויעבר בכל שבטי ישראל.* 
שבע בן בכרי, לפתותם שימליכוהו עליהם:
rashi.eng: *And he passed through all the tribes of Israel.* Sheba the son of Bichri, in order to persuade them to appoint him king over them.

rashi.heb:
*וכל הברים.* 
לא ידעתי מהו:
rashi.eng: *the Berites.* Heb. הברים. I do not know what it is.

notes.732: (tn, Heb): “they.” The following context makes it clear that this refers to Joab and his army.
notes.733: (tc): The LXX has here ἐνοοῦσαν (enoousan, “were devising”), which apparently presupposes the Hebrew word מַחֲשָׁבִים (makhashavim) rather than the MT מַשְׁחִיתִם (mashkhitim, “were destroying”). With a number of other scholars Driver thinks that the Greek variant may preserve the original reading, but this seems to be an unnecessary conclusion (but see S. R. Driver, Notes on the Hebrew Text and the Topography of the Books of Samuel, 346).

rashi.heb:
*ותעמוד בחל.* 
(תרגום:) ואקיפו משריין. ויש פותרים, ותעמוד בחל, לשון (איכה ב ח): חיל וחומה, הפילו החומה החיצונה, ונתחזקה לעמוד על ידי הפנימית:
rashi.eng: *with only its inner wall.* And it stood surrounded by the army. Others interpret ותעמד בחל as an expression similar to חיל וחומה of Lam. 2:8. They felled the outer wall and it [the city] strengthened itself to stand with [only] its inner wall.

rashi.heb:
*האתה יואב.* 
שנאמר בך (לקמן כג ח): יושב בשבת תחכמוני:
rashi.eng: *Are you Joab?.* [Are you the Joab] regarding whom it is said: Who sits in the assembly of the wise?

rashi.heb:
*דבר ידברו בראשונה לאמר.* 
היה לך לדבר לשלום בראשונה, אם שלום יענוך ויפתחו לך, לא היה לך להלחם עליהם:
rashi.eng: *Surely they should have spoken first [to hear what they have] to say.* You first should have spoken to them [to see] if they answer you for peace and open up for you, for then you should not have fought against them.

rashi.heb:
*שאול ישאלו באבל.* 
אם שאלו בני חילך בשלום העיר הזאת, ששמה אבל:
rashi.eng: *had they inquired of Abel.* Had the men of your army inquired of the peace of this city whose name is Abel.

rashi.heb:
*וכן התמו.* 
מיד היו בני העיר משלימים עמכם:
rashi.eng: *so would they have made peace.* Immediately the people of the city would have made peace with you.

notes.734: (tn, Heb): “a city and a mother.” The expression is a hendiadys, meaning that this city was an important one in Israel and had smaller cities dependent on it.

rashi.heb:
*אנכי שלומי אמוני ישראל.* 
אני מבני העיר, ששלמים ונאמנים לישראל ולמלך ומדרש אגדה (בראשית רבה צד ט, ובילקוט שמעוני כא): סרח בת אשר היתה, אני השלמתי נאמן לנאמן, על ידי נגלה ארונו של יוסף למשה, אני הגדתי ליעקב כי יוסף חי:
rashi.eng: *peaceful and faithful to Israel.* I am from those people of the city who are peaceful and faithful to Israel and to the king. Now there is a Midrash Aggadah that she was Serah the daughter of Asher. I am the one who surrendered one faithful to another faithful [i.e., Jospeh to Moses]. Through me Joseph’s casket was revealed to Moses (See Eccl. R. 9:25); and I was the one who notified Jacob that Joseph was yet alive.

notes.735: (tn, Heb): “Far be it, far be it from me.” The expression is clearly emphatic, as may be seen in part by the repetition. P. K. McCarter, however, understands it to be coarser than the translation adopted here. He renders it as “I’ll be damned if…” (II Samuel [AB], 426, 429), which (while it is not a literal translation) may not be too far removed from the way a soldier might have expressed himself.

rashi.heb:
*חלילה חלילה לי.* 
חלילה לי, חלילה למלך:
rashi.eng: *far be it, far be it from me.* Far be it from me, far be it from the king.

rashi.heb:
*נשא ידו במלך בדוד.* 
במלך אפילו אינו דוד, חייב מיתה, ובדוד אפילו אינו מלך, חייב מיתה, וכל שכן במלך בדוד, כך נדרש במדרש קהלת (ט יח):
rashi.eng: *lifted his hand against the king, against David.* [Had he rebelled] against a king, even if he were not David, he would be deserving of death. Or against David, who is a great scholar, even if he were not a king, he would be deserving of death. How much more so against the king against David. This is the manner in which it has been expounded in Midrash Koheleth.

notes.738: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (Joab) has been specified in the translation for clarity.
notes.739: (tn, Heb): “they”; the referent (Joab’s men) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*ותבא האשה אל כל העם בחכמתה.* 
שנינו בתוספתא (תרומות סוף פרק ז): אמרה להם: הואיל והוא נהרג והם נהרגין, תנוהו להם, אם היה יכול להנצל, כגון שהוא מבפנים ואתם מבחוץ, ואתם בסכנה והוא יכול להמלט, אין דוחין נפש מפני נפש להורגו בשביל הצלתכם, אבל עכשיו שגם הוא יהרג עמכם, הואיל ונהרסו החומות ואין כח להמלט, מוטב ימות לבדו ואל תמותו עמו רבי שמעון אומר, כך אמרה להם: המורד במלכות בית דוד חייב מיתה:
rashi.eng: *And the woman came to the people in her wisdom.* We learned in the Tosefta (Terumot ch. 7) that she said to them: Since he and they [the soldiers of the city of Abel] shall be killed, present him to them. If he could conceivably save himself; if he were, for example, on the inside [of the city wall] and you were on the outside, and only you were in a state of danger while he could save himself, one dare not disregard one human life for the sake of another human life by killing him in order to save yourselves. Now, however, that he too will be killed together with you, since the walls have been destroyed and we have no strength to save ourselves it is better that he die alone and you die not with him. R. Simeon stated: This is what she told them: Whosoever rebels against the Davidic dynasty is deserving of death.

rashi.heb:
*ויואב אל כל הצבא.* 
אף על פי שאמר דוד על עמשא (לעיל יט יד): כי שר צבא אשימך תחת יואב, עכשיו שמת עמשא, לא זז יואב ממקומו, ועל ידי יואב הוזקק למנות את חביריו:
rashi.eng: *And Joab was over the entire army.* Although David had said to Amasa: “I will appoint you as general in Joab’s stead” (Above 19:14), now that Amasa was dead Joab did not move from his position. Now on account of Joab he was obliged to also make mention of his associates.

notes.741: (tn, Heb): “Adoram” (so KJV, NAB, NRSV, CEV), but see 1 Kgs 4:6; 5:14.

notes.743: (tn, Heb): “priest for David.” KJV (“a chief ruler about David”) and ASV (“chief minister unto David”) regarded this office as political.

rashi.heb:
*עירא היארי.* 
תרגם יונתן: עירא יאיראה דמן תקוע. וכן הוא קרוי בספר הזה (לקמן כג כו): עירא בן עיקש התקועי. ו'יאירי' נקרא, על שם ששנינו במנחות (פה ב): תקוע אלפא לשמן, ששמן זית מצוי לשם, שממנו מדליקין הנרות:
rashi.eng: *Ira the Jairite.* Jonathan translates: “Ira the Jairite from [the city of] Tekoah,” and so we find him referred to in this book (below 23:26) as Ira the son of Ikkesh the Tekoite. Now he was called the Jairite because we learned in (T.B.) Men: “Tekoah is famous for oil, since olive oil is [abundantly] found there from which we light the candles.”

rashi.heb:
*היה כהן לדוד.* 
לו היה נותן כל מתנות כהונה שלו, כך אמרו רבותינו (עירובין סג א) ופשוטו של מקרא, שעשאו שר ושופט:
rashi.eng: *was a chief official.* He would give him all his priestly gifts. This is what our Rabbis said. However, the simple meaning of the verse is that he appointed him as an official or judge.

notes.744: (tn, Heb): “sought the face of the Lord.”

rashi.heb:
*אל שאול.* 
על עון שאול שנקבר פתאום בהחבא, שגנבוהו אנשי יבש גלעד וקברוהו, ולא נספד לפי כבודו:
rashi.eng: *it is for Saul.* [It is] for the wrong [done] to Saul, for he was buried suddenly and secretively since the people of Jabesh Gilead smuggled him out and buried him without eulogizing him in a manner befitting him.

rashi.heb:
*ואל בית הדמים.* 
שהרג נוב עיר הכהנים:
rashi.eng: *and (also) for his bloody house.* For having killed Nob the priestly city (I Sam. 22:19).

rashi.heb:
*על אשר המית את הגבעונים.* 
כשהרג נוב עיר הכהנים, המית מהם שבעה, שני חוטבי עצים, ושני שואבי מים, ושמש וחזן וסופר, כך מפורש בגמרא ירושלמית בסנהדרין (יז) ורבותינו אמרו: מתוך שהרג את הכהנים שהיו מספיקין להם מזון, העלה עליו הכתוב כאלו המיתם. ואל תתמה שהרי היה הקב"ה תובע כבודו ותובע סרחונו, שכך כתוב (צפניה ב ג): אשר משפטו פעלו באשר משפטו, שם פעלו כך שנינו ביבמות (עח ב):
rashi.eng: *because he put to death the Gibeonites..* When he [Saul] murdered the priestly city of Nob he killed seven of them [Gibeonites]; two wood cutters and two water drawers, an attendant, a carrier, and a scribe. In this manner it is explained in the Jerusalem Talmud Tractate Sanhedrin. But our rabbis (i.e., of T.B.) stated, since he slew the priests who had provided them [the Gibeonites] with food, scripture considers it as though he had slain them. Now do not wonder that the Holy One Blessed be He demands his honor and [simultaneously] demands punishment for his sin, for so it is written: “that have executed his judgment (אשר משפטו פעלו)” (Zeph. 2:3). Where there is found His judgment there can also be found His execution.

rashi.heb:
*ויאמר אליהם.* 
דברי ריצוי, שיעברו על מדותיהם וימחלו לשאול ולביתו:
rashi.eng: *and he said to them.* Words of appeasement in order that they forgo retaliation and pardon Saul and his household.

rashi.heb:
*והגבעונים לא מבני ישראל המה.* 
כלומר והן הראו בעצמם מדת אכזריות, שאינן מזרעו של אברהם אבינו, ואינן ראויין לידבק בישראל, ולכך גזר עליהם דוד שלא יבואו בקהל, אמר: שלשה סימנים יש באומה זו, רחמנים וביישנים וגומלי חסדים, מי שיש בו שלשה סימנים הללו, ראוי לידבק בו:
rashi.eng: *Now the Gibeonites were not of the children of Israel.* That is, they exhibited the characteristic of being merciless [which gave indication] that they are not of the seed of Abraham. As a result David decreed upon them that they may not enter the [Israelite] community. He said: This [Israelite] nation possesses three signs; they are compassionate, they are bashful, and they are benevolent. [Only] whosoever possesses these three virtues is worthy of joining it.

rashi.heb:
*נשבעו להם.* 
בימי יהושע כשנתנום חוטבי עצים ושואבי מים למזבח (יהושע ט טו):
rashi.eng: *had sworn to them.* In the days of Joshua when they were appointed wood cutters and water drawers for the altar.

rashi.heb:
*בקנאתו לבני ישראל.* 
בתתו לב לנקות ולטהר את ישראל ולעשות צרכיהם, בקש להרגם וקנאה זו לטובה, כמו (במדבר יא כט:) המקנא אתה לי ; וכן (מלכים-ב י טז): בקנאתי לה' דיהוא זהו פשוטו. ולפי מדרשו, לא אמר להרוג אלא את הכהנים, וקנאה זו האמורה כאן, אינה לטובה כי אם לרעה, שידע שלא תמשוך מלכותו מיום שלא שמר מצות הקב"ה בעמלק, ומאז נתקנא בהם:
rashi.eng: *in his zeal for the sake of the children.* When he made up his mind [lit., his heart] to cleanse and purify Israel and to provide for their needs, he sought to kill them. Now the קנאה of the verse is meant in a positive sense, similar to: “are you zealous (המקנא) for my sake” (Num. 11:29) or: “my zeal (בקנאתי) for God” (2 Kings 10:16) mentioned in connection with Jehu. This is the simple explanation. According to the Midrashic explanation, however, he commanded only to kill the priests, thus the envy stated here is not for good but for bad. He knew that his kingdom would be discontinued from the day he failed to heed the command of the Holy One Blessed be He concerning the Amalekites and there upon became jealous of them [the priests who had harbored David].

notes.747: (tn): After the preceding imperfect verbal form, the subordinated imperative indicates purpose/result. S. R. Driver comments, “…the imper. is used instead of the more normal voluntative, for the purpose of expressing with somewhat greater force the intention of the previous verb” (S. R. Driver, Notes on the Hebrew Text and the Topography of the Books of Samuel, 350).

rashi.heb:
*וברכו את נחלת ה'.* 
התפללו עליהם:
rashi.eng: *bless the inheritance of the Lord.* Pray for them.

notes.748: (tc): The translation follows the Qere and several medieval Hebrew mss in reading לָנוּ (lanu, “to us”) rather than the MT לִי (li, “to me”). But for a contrary opinion see S. R. Driver, Notes on the Hebrew Text and the Topography of the Books of Samuel, 53, 350.
notes.750: (tn, Heb): “and he said”; the referent (David) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*אין לנו כסף וזהב עם שאול.* 
כי אם נפשות, ביקש לפייסם בממון, ולא רצו, אמר שמא הם מתביישין זה מזה, הלך ופייס כל אחד ואחד לעצמו, ולא נתפייסו, לכך כתיב: אין לי כסף וזהב וגו', לשון יחיד, זו ראיתי בירושלמי (סנהדרין ו ז):
rashi.eng: *We have no matters of silver and gold.* Only of lives. He sought to appease them with money but they refused. He said [to himself], Perhaps they are ashamed before one another [to consent to take money]. He therefore went and appealed each one individually but they nevertheless refused to be appeased. It is on account of this that it is written, “I have no matters of silver and gold, etc.” in singular form. This I have seen in the Jerusalem Talmud.

rashi.heb:
*ואין לנו איש להמית.* 
בכל שאר בני ישראל, שלא חטאו לנו:
rashi.eng: *and we [care not] to put to death.* Any of the other people of Israel who have not wronged us.

rashi.heb:
*ואשר דמה לנו נשמדנו.* 
אשר אמר בלבו, שנשמדנו על ידו מהתיצב וגו', שחשב להשמידנו:
rashi.eng: *and who devised against us that we be destroyed.* who planned in his heart, by whom we have been destroyed from remaining etc. i.e., who devised to destroy us.

rashi.heb:
*דמה לנו.* 
חשב עלינו להשמידנו:
rashi.eng: *devised against us.* He devised against us to destroy us.

notes.751: (tn): The exact nature of this execution is not altogether clear. The verb יָקַע (yaqa’) basically means “to dislocate” or “alienate.” In Gen 32:26 it is used of the dislocation of Jacob’s thigh. Figuratively it can refer to the removal of an individual from a group (e.g., Jer 6:8; Ezek 23:17) or to a type of punishment the specific identity of which is uncertain (e.g., here and Num 25:4); cf. NAB “dismember them”; NIV “to be killed and exposed.”
notes.752: (tc): The LXX reads “at Gibeon on the mountain of the Lord” (cf. 21:9). The present translation follows the MT, although a number of recent English translations follow the LXX reading here (e.g., NAB, NRSV, NLT).

rashi.heb:
*והוקענום.* 
תלייה:
rashi.eng: *hang them.* Heb. והוקענום, an expression meaning hanging.

rashi.heb:
*לה'.* 
לשמו של מקום, להודיע משפטו:
rashi.eng: *for the sake of.* for the Lord’s name, in order to publicize His judgement.

rashi.heb:
*בחיר ה'.* 
בת קול יצאה ואמרה: בחיר ה' (ברכות יב ב):
rashi.eng: *chosen of the Lord.* a heavenly voice came forth and declared: the chosen of the Lord.

rashi.heb:
*ויחמל המלך.* 
בקש רחמים שלא יקלטנו הארון, שהעבירם לפני הארון, כל שהארון קולטו, למיתה (יבמות עט א):
rashi.eng: *took pity.* He begged that the ark should not clutch him; for he led them all in front of the ark, and those that the ark clutched [were selected] for death.

notes.753: (tc): The MT reads “Michal” here, but two Hebrew manuscripts read “Merab,” along with some LXX manuscripts. Cf. 1 Sam 18:19.

rashi.heb:
*בני מיכל בת שאול אשר ילדה לעדריאל.* 
וכי מיכל ילדה, והלא מירב ילדה לו, אלא מירב ילדה, ומיכל גדלה, לפיכך נקרא על שמה, והמגדל יתום ויתומה בתוך ביתו, כאלו ילדו ונקרא על שמו (סנהדרין יט ב):
rashi.eng: *the five sons of Michal.* Now did Michal bear them? Did not Merab rear them? We conclude that Merab bore them but Michal raised them and they therefore were called after her name; for one who raises an orphan in his house is as if he had begotten them and he is called after his name.

notes.754: (tc): The translation follows the Qere and several medieval Hebrew mss in reading שְׁבַעְתָּם (sh�va’tam, “the seven of them”) rather than MT שִׁבַעְתִּים (shiva’tim, “seventy”).
notes.756: (tc): The translation follows the Qere and many medieval Hebrew mss in reading בִּתְחִלַּת (bithkhillat, “in the beginning”) rather than MT תְחִלַּת (t�khillat, “beginning of”).

rashi.heb:
*בתחלת קציר.* 
בימי ניסן:
rashi.eng: *at the beginning of the barley harvest.* In the days of Nissan.

notes.757: (tn, Heb): “until water was poured on them from the sky.”

rashi.heb:
*עד נתך מים.* 
בימות הגשמים בתשרי, שלא נתנו לקבורה והלא כתיב (דברים כא כג): לא תלין נבלתו, אלא אמרו מוטב תיעקר אות אחת מן התורה, ויתקדש שם שמים בפרהסיא, שהיו עוברין ושבין אומרים: מה טיבן של אלו, אומרים להם: מבני מלכים הם, ומה עשו, פשטו ידם בגרים גרורים, אומרים: אין לך אומה ראויה לידבק בה כאומה זו (יבמות עט א):
rashi.eng: *Until water was poured.* In the rainy season of Tishrei; for they were not given over for burial. But it is not written: “You shall not allow his body to remain overnight” (Deut. 21:22)? However they said: It is preferable that one letter of the Torah be uprooted so that the Divine Name be publicly hallowed for when passersby would inquire: Who are these? They would say to them: They are princes. And what did they do? They stretched out their hands against those who attached themselves but were [proselytes] not accepted. They would then say: There is no nation that one ought to join like this one.

notes.760: (tn, Heb): “David.” For stylistic reasons the name has been replaced by the pronoun (“he”) in the translation.
notes.761: (tn, Heb): “the bones of Saul and the bones of Jonathan his son.” See also v. 13.
notes.764: (tc): Against the MT, this word is better read without the definite article. The MT reading is probably here the result of wrong word division, with the letter ה (he) belonging with the preceding word שָׁם (sham) as the he directive (i.e., שָׁמָּה, samah, “to there”).

rashi.heb:
*ויקח את עצמות שאול.* 
שנאמר לו עליהם 'אל שאול', שלא נספד כהלכה:
rashi.eng: *and he took the bones of Saul.* For he was told regarding them [Saul and Jonathan]: It is for Saul, since he was not eulogized properly.

notes.768: (tn, Heb): “he”; the referent (David) has been specified in the translation for clarity.

rashi.heb:
*ויאספו את עצמות.* 
שבעה המוקעין:
rashi.eng: *and they gathered the bones.* of the seven who were hanged here.

notes.769: (tc): Many medieval Hebrew mss have here כְּכֹל (k�khol, “according to all”).
notes.770: (tn, Heb): “was entreated.” The verb is an example of the so-called niphal tolerativum, with the sense that God allowed himself to be supplicated through prayer (cf. GKC 137 �51.c).

rashi.heb:
*כל אשר צוה המלך.* 
להספיד עליהם בכל ערי ישראל:
rashi.eng: *all that the king commanded them.* To eulogize them in all of Israel’s cities.

notes.772: (tn): This name has the definite article and may be intended to refer to a group of people rather than a single individual with this name.
notes.773: (tn): This is the only occurrence of this Hebrew word in the OT. Its precise meaning is therefore somewhat uncertain. As early as the LXX the word was understood to refer to a “spear,” and this seems to be the most likely possibility. Some scholars have proposed emending the text of 2 Sam 21:16 to כוֹבַעוֹ (khova’o; “his helmet”), but in spite of the fact that the word “helmet” appears in 1 Sam 17:5, there is not much evidence for reading that word here.
notes.774: (tn): Either the word “shekels” should be supplied here, or the Hebrew word מִשְׁקַל (mishqal, “weight”) right before “bronze” is a corrupted form of the word for shekel. If the latter is the case the problem probably resulted from another occurrence of the word מִשְׁקַל just four words earlier in the verse. Three hundred bronze shekels would have weighed about 7.5 pounds (3.4 kg).
notes.775: (tn): The Hebrew text reads simply “a new [thing],” prompting one to ask “A new what?” Several possibilities have been proposed to resolve the problem: perhaps a word has dropped out of the Hebrew text here; or perhaps the word “new” is the result of misreading a different, less common, word; or perhaps a word (e.g., “sword,” so KJV, NAB, NASB, NIV, CEV, NLT) is simply to be inferred. The translation generally follows the latter possibility, while at the same time being deliberately nonspecific (“weapon”).

rashi.heb:
*ומשקל קינו.* 
הוא כמו תיק שבראש בית יד הרומח שקורין ארישטויי"ל בלע"ז, ועשוי ככובע, ויש דוגמתו בזבחים (פח ב, עיין שיטה מקובצת שם): רמוני המעיל למה הם דומין, כמין קולסות שבראשי התינוקות, 'קולסות' היילמ"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *and the weight of his spear.* Heb. קינו. It is like the sheath at the end of the handle of the spear which is called arestojjl in French, and is made like the hat. Its parallel is [found in T.B.] Zebachim: “What are the blossoms of the robe like, [they are] like the helmets that are on the heads of infants.” Now קולסות are heajjlmes in French.

rashi.heb:
*והוא חגור.* 
חגורה חדשה ושמעתי, שאותו היום נתחנך ללבוש כלי מלחמה, ודרך המחונכים לעשות נצחון וגבורה ביום חינוכם, לקנות שם, לכך ויאמר להכות את דוד:
rashi.eng: *and he was girded.* With a new outfit. Now I heard that on that day he was initiated into the wearing of armor. Since it is common for the [newly] initiated to perform [an act of] victory and heroism on the day of their initiation in order to acquire a reputation, he therefore thought to smite David.

rashi.heb:
*ויעזר לו.* 
שעזרו בתפלה, כדאיתא בחלק (סנהדרין צה א):
rashi.eng: *aided him.* He aided him through prayer, as is found in the chapter of Chelek [the 10th perek of Sanhedrin].

rashi.heb:
*ותהי עוד המלחמה.* 
כבר קדמה זו לכולן, ולא מנאה כאן, אלא לצרף מיתת ארבעה בני ערפה:
rashi.eng: *And there was war again.* This one preceded them all, but is mentioned here only to connect the deaths of the four sons of Orpah.

notes.776: (tn, Heb): “Jaare-Oregim,” but the second word, which means “weavers,” is probably accidentally included. It appears at the end of the verse. The term is omitted in the parallel account in 1 Chr 20:5, which has simply “Jair.”
notes.777: (sn): The Hebrew text as it stands reads, “Elhanan son of Jaare-Oregim the Bethlehemite killed Goliath the Gittite.” Who killed Goliath the Gittite? According to 1 Sam 17:4-58 it was David who killed Goliath, but according to the MT of 2 Sam 21:19 it was Elhanan who killed him. Many scholars believe that the two passages are hopelessly at variance with one another. Others have proposed various solutions to the difficulty, such as identifying David with Elhanan or positing the existence of two Goliaths. But in all likelihood the problem is the result of difficulties in the textual transmission of the Samuel passage; in fact, from a text-critical point of view the books of Samuel are the most poorly preserved of all the books of the Hebrew Bible. The parallel passage in 1 Chr 20:5 reads, “Elhanan son of Jair killed Lahmi the brother of Goliath.” Both versions are textually corrupt. The Chronicles text has misread “Bethlehemite” (בֵּית הַלַּחְמִי, bet hallakhmi) as the accusative sign followed by a proper name אֶת לַחְמִי (’et lakhmi). (See the note at 1 Chr 20:5.) The Samuel text misread the word for “brother” (אַח, ’akh) as the accusative sign (אֵת, ’et), thereby giving the impression that Elhanan, not David, killed Goliath. Thus in all probability the original text read, “Elhanan son of Jair the Bethlehemite killed the brother of Goliath.”

rashi.heb:
*אלחנן.* 
דוד:
rashi.eng: *Elhanan.* David.

rashi.heb:
*בן יערי אורגים.* 
שהיו משפחתו אורגים פרוכת למקדש הקרוי יער:
rashi.eng: *the son of Jaare-oregim.* Heb. אורגים, lit. weavers. For his family wove curtains for the Holy Temple which was called Jaar (see I Kings 10:17, and 10:21).

rashi.heb:
*כמנור אורגים.* 
(תרגום:) כאכסן דגרדאין, הקרוי אינשובל"א בלע"ז, תבא אריגה ותעמוד כנגד אריגה:
rashi.eng: *as the weavers’ beam.* As a weaver’s beam which is called esoble in French.

rashi.heb:
*איש מדון.* 
כתרגומו: גבר דמשחן. שאין עיקר התיבה אלא מ"ם ודלי"ת, כמו (תהלים סה ח) מ'שאון' שי"ן ואל"ף (בראשית יז ד): ומ'המון', ה"א ומ"ם. ובדברי הימים (א יא כג) כתיב: איש מדה, כלומר גבוה מאוד, שאומדין כמה מדתו:
rashi.eng: *a man of stature.* Heb. איש מדין. As its Targum: “A man of measure,” for the root of the word is basically the מ and ד [from מדה, a measure], just as in משאון of Ps. 65:8 [where it is the] ש and א, and מהמון [where it is the] ה and מ. Now in I Chron. 11:23 it is [expressly] written: “a man of measure (איש מדה) ”; that is a man so tall that one [is inclined] to estimate how tall he is.

rashi.heb:
*שש ושש וגו'.* 
פירשו רבותינו בבכורות (מה ב) שהוצרך לומר עשרים וארבע, שלא תאמר אצבעות שתי ידיו אינן אלא שש, ואצבעות רגליו אינן אלא שש, לכך נאמר עשרים וארבע ואם כתב עשרים וארבע ולא אמר שש ושש, הייתי אומר שבעה באחת, וחמשה באחת, ומהו 'מספר', שכולן היו נספרות בסדר האצבעות בגב היד:
rashi.eng: *six and six totalling twenty-four.* Our Rabbis have explained in [T.B.] Bechoroth that it was necessary to state twenty-four so that you should not say that the fingers of his two hands were only six [three on each hand], and the toes of his feet were only six; it therefore mentions twenty-four. Now if it had mentioned twenty-four and not six and six we would say [that he perhaps had] seven on one hand and five on the other. Now what does מספר imply? That all are [to be] counted in the order of fingers on the hand.

notes.781: (sn): In this long song of thanks, David affirms that God is his faithful protector. He recalls in highly poetic fashion how God intervened in awesome power and delivered him from death. His experience demonstrates that God vindicates those who are blameless and remain loyal to him. True to his promises, God gives the king victory on the battlefield and enables him to subdue nations. A parallel version of the song appears in Ps 18.
notes.783: (tn, Heb): “in the day,” or “at the time.”
notes.785: (tn, Heb): “and from the hand of Saul.”

rashi.heb:
*ביום הציל ה' אותו.* 
לעת זקנתו, לאחר שעברו עליו כל צרותיו ונצול מכולם:
rashi.eng: *In the day that the Lord delivered him.* In his later years when all his troubles had passed over him and he had been saved from them all.

rashi.heb:
*ומכף שאול.* 
והלא שאול בכלל היה, אלא שהיה אויבו ורודפו מכולם כיוצא בו (לעיל ב ל): תשעה עשר איש ועשהאל, כיוצא בו (יהושע ב א): לכו ראו את הארץ ואת יריחו וכיוצא בו (מלכים-א יא א): והמלך שלמה אהב נשים נכריות ואת בת פרעה (מלכים-א יא א):
rashi.eng: *and out of the hand of Saul.* But is not Saul included [among his enemies]? However he was his enemy and pursuer to a greater degree than all the others [and was therefore cited separately]. Similarly [we find]: “nineteen men and Asahel” (above 2:30). Similarly, “And King Solomon loved foreign women, and the daughter of Pharoah” (I Kings 11:1).

notes.786: (tn): Traditionally “is my rock”; CEV “mighty rock”; TEV “is my protector.” This metaphor pictures God as a rocky, relatively inaccessible summit, where one would be able to find protection from enemies. See 1 Sam 23:25, 28.
notes.787: (tn): Traditionally “my fortress”; TEV “my strong fortress”; NCV “my protection.” My stronghold. David often found safety in such strongholds. See 1 Sam 22:4-5; 24:22; 2 Sam 5:9, 17; 23:14.

rashi.heb:
*סלעי ומצודתי.* 
לשון חוזק הם, 'סלע' כמשמעו, 'מצודה' היא מצודת יערים, שקורין פליישאי"ן בלע"ז ועל שם הנס שנעשה לו בסלע המחלוקת (שמואל-א כג ח), והמצדות בחורשה:
rashi.eng: *my rock and my fortress.* Heb. סלעי ומצדתי. They are expressions of strength; סלעי, rock, requires no explanation; מצדתי, fortress refers to the fortresses of the forests which are called pleisiz in French. This is an allusion to the miracle which was performed on his behalf at the rock of Machloketh (I Sam. 23:28), and at the fortresses at Harsha (I Sam. 23:15 19).

rashi.heb:
*ומפלטי לי.* 
מפלטי עם צבא ישראל במלחמה, ופעמים שהוא מפלט לי כשאני לבדי, כגון מן ישבי בנוב (לעיל כא יז):
rashi.eng: *and a rescuer to me..* [He was] my rescuer [when I was] together with the army of Israel engaged in battle. On occasions, [however,] he rescued me when I was alone, as from Ishbi in Nob (Above 21:16).

notes.788: (tc): The translation (along with many English versions, e.g., NAB, NIV, NRSV, NLT) follows the LXX in reading אֱלֹהִי (’elohi, “my God”) rather than MT’s אֱלֹהֵי (’elohe, “the God of”). See Ps 18:2.
notes.790: (tn, Heb): “the horn of my salvation,” or “my saving horn.” Though some see “horn” as referring to a horn-shaped peak of a hill, or to the “horns” of an altar where one could find refuge, it is more likely that the horn of an ox underlies the metaphor (see Deut 33:17; 1 Kgs 22:11; Ps 92:10). The horn of the wild ox is frequently a metaphor for military strength; the idiom “exalt the horn” signifies military victory (see 1 Sam 2:10; Pss 89:17, 24; 92:10; Lam 2:17). In the ancient Near East powerful warrior-kings would sometimes compare themselves to a goring bull that uses its horns to kill its enemies. For examples, see P. Miller, “El the Warrior,” HTR 60 (1967): 422-25, and R. B. Chisholm, “An Exegetical and Theological Study of Psalm 18/2 Samuel 22” (Th.D. diss., Dallas Theological Seminary, 1983), 135-36. 2 Sam 22:3 uses the metaphor of the horn in a slightly different manner. Here the Lord himself is compared to a horn. He is to the psalmist what the horn is to the ox, a source of defense and victory.
notes.791: (tn): The parallel version of the song in Ps 18 does not include this last line.

rashi.heb:
*צורי.* 
לשון סלע, שהסלע מחסה לעוברי דרך, מן המטר והרוחות, אבריאמ"ש בלע"ז:
rashi.eng: *my rock.* Heb. צורי, synonymous with סלע. [He was his rock] since the rock protects travelers from the [force of] the rain and the wind, abriemant in French.

rashi.heb:
*אחסה.* 
לשון כיסוי, שהייתי מתכסה לעזרה:
rashi.eng: *under whom I take cover.* Heb. אחסה, an expression of covering; I would cover myself waiting for [His] aid.

rashi.heb:
*משגבי.* 
סומכני:
rashi.eng: *my support.* Heb. משגבי, my support.

rashi.heb:
*ומנוסי.* 
שהייתי נס אליו לעזרה:
rashi.eng: *and my refuge.* For I would run to Him for aid.

notes.792: (tn): In this song of thanksgiving, where David recalls how the Lord delivered him, the prefixed verbal form is best understood as a preterite indicating past tense (cf. CEV “I prayed”), not an imperfect (as in many English versions).
notes.793: (tn, Heb): “worthy of praise, I cried out [to] the Lord.” Some take מְהֻלָּל (m�hullal, “worthy of praise”) with what precedes and translate, “the praiseworthy one,” or “praiseworthy.” However, the various epithets in vv. 1-2 have the first person pronominal suffix, unlike מְהֻלָּל. If one follows the traditional verse division and takes מְהֻלָּל with what follows, it is best understood as substantival and as appositional to יְהוָה (y�hvah, “Yahweh”), resulting in “[to the] praiseworthy one I cried out, [to the] Lord.”

rashi.heb:
*מהולל אקרא ה'.* 
כתרגומו ; בקראי לו אהודנו, לפי כי מאויבי אני בוטח שאושע ויתכן לפתור אקרא ואושע, לשון 'הוה':
rashi.eng: *With praise I call to the Lord.* Just as its Targum. Upon calling Him I [already] praise Him, for I am confidant that I will be saved. It is also plausible to interpret it: ‘I call and I am saved,’ in present sense.

notes.794: (tn): The noun נַחַל (nakhal) usually refers to a river or stream, but in this context the plural form likely refers to the currents of the sea (see vv. 15-16).
notes.795: (tn): The noun בְלִיַּעַל (b�liyya’al) is used here as an epithet for death. Elsewhere it is a common noun meaning “wickedness, uselessness” (see HALOT 133-34 s.v. בְּלִיַּעַל). It is often associated with rebellion against authority and other crimes that result in societal disorder and anarchy. The phrase “man/son of wickedness” refers to one who opposes God and the order he has established. The term becomes an appropriate title for death, which, through human forces, launches an attack against God’s chosen servant.
notes.796: (tn): In this poetic narrative context the prefixed verbal form is best understood as a preterite indicating past tense, not an imperfect. (Note the perfect verbal form in the parallel/preceding line.) The verb בָּעַת (ba’at) sometimes by metonymy carries the nuance “frighten,” but the parallelism (note “engulfed” in the preceding line) favors the meaning “overwhelm” here.

rashi.heb:
*אפפוני.* 
הקיפוני:
rashi.eng: *have encompassed me.* Heb. אפפני, have encompassed me.

rashi.heb:
*משברי מות.* 
כתרגומו: כאתא דיתבא על מתברא, כן שם מושב האבנים שהאשה יולדת שם:
rashi.eng: *pains of death.* As its Targum: ‘Like a woman who sits on the travailing chair.’ This (משבר) is the term for the stone seat on which a woman gives birth.

rashi.heb:
*נחלי.* 
גייסות שוטפות כנחל:
rashi.eng: *streams of scoundrels.* Armies that overflow like a stream.

notes.797: (tn): “Sheol,” personified here as David’s enemy, is the underworld, place of the dead in primitive Hebrew cosmology.

rashi.heb:
*חבלי.* 
כתרגומו: משרית, כמו (שמואל-א י ה): חבל נביאים:
rashi.eng: *bands.* Heb. חבלי, as its Targum: Bands, similar to: “Bands of prophets (חבל נביאים)” of I Sam. 10:10.

rashi.heb:
*קדמוני.* 
באו לפני:
rashi.eng: *confronted me.* came before me.
